H_hierarchical.evidence: The software is decomposed into delivery, pick-up, reset, and fault-protection subsystems, and the delivery subsystem has an internal multi-step sub-flow.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Guard logic includes delivery-signal detection, occupied-position branching, target-position reach checks, interlock logic, and an any-limit-switch safety condition over multiple inputs.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Transitions drive X/Y stepper motors, reverse/forward Z-axis fork motion, display operation errors and position numbers, actuate relay KM3, and run reset; actions are mostly concrete PLC outputs.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper defines a fault-protection subsystem and limit-switch/error paths that display an error, cut stepper power, or reset the stacker to the zero position.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Delivery/reset state flow is in the software-design section, while actuator mappings, sensor guards, relay actions, and interlock details are in earlier hardware sections.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as interlock, emergency shutdown, self-resetting, and fault protection imply control rules beyond plain event names.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are described narratively across prose and hardware mapping rather than as a co-located state-action table.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The limit-switch fault condition is effectively a boolean OR over multiple PLC limit inputs, and the interlock encodes mutually exclusive drive conditions.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: The paper decomposes the controller into subsystems and sub-flow steps, but does not give parent states independent entry/during/exit behavior beyond child steps.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Limit-switch/failure handling is described as a system-level protection rule that cuts motor power regardless of the current movement step.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is a shallow composite delivery subsystem with a default start from delivery signal to position reading, but no deep pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Boolean guard consistency matters for limit-switch OR conditions and forward/reverse interlocks, but the paper lacks rich arithmetic guard formulas.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Fault/limit protection applies across several motion substates, so a forced transition or parent-level monitor would avoid duplicating the same safety edge.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Some outputs are abstract at the NL level, such as operation-error indication and current-position display, though most actions map to concrete motors, lamps, and relays.

When the PLC receives any of the limit switch signal input
one_line_pitch: A compact industrial PLC stacker case with subsystem hierarchy, multi-sensor guards, motor/display/relay actions, and cross-cutting limit-switch protection that exposes known guard/action/context weaknesses of prior baselines.
rationale: This is a strong stress-test sample because the paper gives a real sequential storage controller rather than only I/O wiring: the delivery sub-flow contains occupancy checks, X/Y/Z motion steps, fork placement, reset, and fault handling. Its weakest-baseline features are concentrated in guards, actions, and recovery: multi-input safety guards, interlock semantics, PLC output side effects, and system-level power cut/reset behavior. The hierarchy is shallow, but the cross-section split between software flow and hardware I/O mapping makes it difficult for single-pass Umple-style synthesis to preserve semantics.
